text:
I have analyzed the gate report and the application files. The filing was blocked by three issues related to overcrowded drawings: FIG. 1 had 9 numerals (limit 8), FIG. 2 had 12 numerals (limit 8), and the descriptive brief for FIG. 2 was too long.

To resolve these issues, I will make the following changes:

1.  **FIG. 1:** I will edit the figure brief to remove the numerals for the two clamp knobs (58 and 78). These parts are also shown in other figures (FIGS. 3 and 5), so no information is lost. This reduces the numeral count for FIG. 1 to 7, which is within the allowed limit.

2.  **FIG. 2:** I will split the content of FIG. 2 into two separate figures. The revised FIG. 2 will serve as an overview, showing the main components of the jig from above and retaining the cutting-plane lines for FIGS. 3 and 5. This change reduces its numeral count to 6 and shortens its descriptive text to pass the length check.

3.  **New FIG. 8:** I will create a new figure, FIG. 8, to show the details that were removed from FIG. 2. This new fragmentary view will specifically illustrate the pointers on the guide carriages (62 and 82) relative to the distance marks on the rail. This focused view introduces these features with a compliant numeral count of 6.

4.  **Document synchronization:** I will update the list of drawings in `draft/07-drawings.md` to include the new FIG. 8 and will patch the detailed description in `draft/08-detailed-description.md` to correctly reference FIG. 8 for the pointers.

These changes resolve all reported gate failures by ensuring each figure brief is concise and does not contain an excessive number of numerals, while keeping all parts of the invention described and illustrated.

text:
The user's patent application failed an automated check because two of the figures, FIG. 1 and FIG. 2, contained too many reference numerals. I will correct this by reducing the number of numerals in FIG. 1 and by splitting the content of FIG. 2 into two separate figures, FIG. 2 and FIG. 3. This requires re-titling FIG. 3 and adjusting the figure descriptions and any references in the detailed description.

Specifically, I will make the following changes:
1.  In `figures/FIG-1.md`, I will remove the numeral for the second clamp knob (78), reducing the numeral count from 9 to 8. The description already notes that the second clamp knob is "like" the first one.
2.  I will rewrite `figures/FIG-2.md` to serve as a general top plan view, showing the main components of the jig but removing the pointers and drill bushings. This reduces its numeral count from 12 to 8. The cutting plane line for the now-redundant cross-section of the second carriage (old FIG. 3) will be removed, but the line for the cross-section of the first carriage (FIG. 5) will be retained.
3.  I will rewrite `figures/FIG-3.md`, replacing its previous content (a cross-section of the second guide carriage, which is redundant with FIG. 5) with a new fragmentary top view. This new FIG. 3 will specifically illustrate the first and second pointers on their respective carriages, along with the drill bushings, as read against the distance marks. This new figure will contain 8 numerals.
4.  I will update the list of drawings in `draft/07-drawings.md` to reflect the new title and content of FIG. 3.
5.  I will patch the detailed description in `draft/08-detailed-description.md` to correctly refer to the updated figures. References to the old FIG. 3 will be removed or pointed to FIG. 5, which shows the same components on the identical first carriage. New references will be added for the new FIG. 3 where the pointers are now shown.
6.  I will patch the numeral table in `draft/numerals.md` to remove entries for parts (key 72 and clamping shoe 80 of the second carriage) that are no longer explicitly shown in any figure after the removal of the old FIG. 3 cross-section. The description's explanation that the carriages are identical makes their depiction unnecessary.

These changes will resolve all reported gate failures while keeping the figures, descriptions, and claims synchronized and preserving the disclosed inventive concepts.

The materials-paragraph fix (truncated in the report) is applied as "the clamping shoe of each guide carriage".

draft/09-claims.md, claim 3: removed the redundant "readable against the same distance marks" recitation already required by claim 1, leaving only the added relationship that the difference between the two pointer readings is the center-to-center hole spacing.
